_readme: The spots in Live TV's breaks (B, 25 Oct 2026; step 4 of PLAN-voidtv-home-and-spots). donate: the donation spot, at most one an hour per channel, never on kids channels or kids mornings; it names CASH and has the Donate button (the page's DONATE link). tips and know: how voidtv.net works. trivia: TV trivia, shown with Did you know? Every line here is read by the next build; edit, add or remove lines by hand. Keep each line short (under about 140 characters), true, and free of show or studio claims you cannot stand behind.

donate.line: No ads sold, ever. voidtv.net runs on donations. $5 when you can.

tips: Change channels: tap CH, or swipe the picture.
See what's on later: open the Guide.
Like this show? Open it and start from episode one.
Save a show to Mine with the bookmark.
Tap a color in the guide to see only that kind of show.
know: Everything here plays from the Internet Archive.
Live TV is the same for everyone, at the same moment.
New shows join Live TV every Monday.
No account, no sign up, no ads sold.
Each show page has every episode we have, in order.
trivia: The first TV remote, Zenith's Lazy Bones from 1950, was wired to the set.
Seinfeld's pilot was called The Seinfeld Chronicles.
The Simpsons started as short cartoons on The Tracey Ullman Show in 1987.
M*A*S*H ran 11 seasons, far longer than the Korean War it was set in.
More than 100 million Americans watched the M*A*S*H finale in 1983.
Gilligan's Island ran only three seasons, from 1964 to 1967.
Star Trek was cancelled after three seasons. Reruns made it a classic.
Doctor Who first aired in November 1963, the day after President Kennedy was shot.
TARDIS stands for Time And Relative Dimension In Space.
Sesame Street premiered in 1969.
Rod Serling wrote or co-wrote 92 of The Twilight Zone's 156 episodes.
Cheers almost got cancelled in its first season. It ran 11.
Frasier spun off from Cheers and also ran 11 seasons.
The X-Files filmed its first five seasons in Vancouver.
Futurama has been cancelled twice and brought back twice.
Family Guy was cancelled in 2002 and came back after strong DVD sales and reruns.
Mister Rogers' Neighborhood ran on PBS from 1968 to 2001.
The first TV commercial in the US aired in 1941: a Bulova watch ad.
The Andy Griffith Show began as a spin-off of The Danny Thomas Show.
Saturday Night Live first aired in October 1975.
Bob Ross made 403 episodes of The Joy of Painting.
Bob Ross usually painted each picture three times: before, during and after taping.
Scooby-Doo, Where Are You! premiered in 1969.
The Flintstones was the first prime-time animated sitcom, in 1960.
Space Ghost Coast to Coast reused animation from the 1966 Space Ghost cartoon.
Beavis and Butt-Head began on MTV's Liquid Television.
Twin Peaks was filmed around Snoqualmie and North Bend, Washington.
The US Office was adapted from the British series by Ricky Gervais and Stephen Merchant.
Columbo's famous raincoat belonged to Peter Falk himself.
Much of the dialogue on Curb Your Enthusiasm is improvised from an outline.
The Muppet Show was made in England, at ATV's studios in Elstree.
I Love Lucy was one of the first shows filmed with three cameras before a studio audience.
